title: hosted-api-capacity-playbook-tokens-qps-headroom-2026
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the methodology, assumptions, and concrete headroom targets for Redwood’s Hosted API peak capacity planning (tokens/sec and QPS). It covers: regional capacity sizing, GPU fleet allocation, utilization targets, emergency headroom, and operational triggers for autoscaling and failover. The goal is to ensure SLAs for 99th pct latency during bursts while keeping steady-state cost efficiency.

Scope and motivation:
- Scope: Hosted API public endpoints for text generation and embeddings across all production regions. Excludes Dedicated and Private (those have separate runbooks).
- Why: Recent traffic patterns show increasingly bursty token demand from a small set of high-volume customers and partner workloads. We need a simple, repeatable headroom policy so SRE/infra can: (a) size monthly capacity purchases, (b) tune autoscaling policies, (c) set cross-region fallback priorities.

Key definitions (used in equations below):
- QPS: requests per second (for generation calls).
- tokens/sec: emitted tokens per second aggregated across all concurrent requests.
- peak window: 5-minute sliding window used for planning (typical for SLA checks).
- headroom factor (HF): multiplier applied to observed peak to provision buffer (e.g., HF = 1.5).
- usable GPU capacity (UGC): estimated tokens/sec a single GPU can sustain at target p50/p95 latency for a given model mix and sequence length distribution.

Assumptions (baseline month):
- Model mix: 60% Llama-3-70B-8k quantized, 30% Llama-3-13B, 10% embeddings/small models.
- Avg tokens per request: 120 tokens (gen workflows) during peaks; embeddings are counted separately as "units" converted to tokens/sec using our cost model.
- Typical concurrency to QPS ratio: avg token generation rate per request = tokens_per_req * 1 / avg_generation_time; we use tokens/sec aggregation to avoid per-request variation.
- Measured UGC (production profiling):
  - A100-80GB (fp16/quantized): 14k tokens/sec at p50 latency target, sustainable up to 70% utilization before latency degradation.
  - H100-80GB: 22k tokens/sec at p50 latency target, sustainable up to 75% utilization.
  - 8-bit quantized M60-equivalents (in private clusters): 6k tokens/sec.

Regional sizing methodology (step-by-step):
1) Observe historical 95th pct tokens/sec per region over trailing 30-day window (T30-95).
2) Apply growth allowance: pick conservative monthly growth multiplier (g). For Q4 planning use g = 1.12 (12% month-over-month sensitive customers).
3) Determine required tokens/sec = T30-95 * g.
4) Apply headroom factor HF to get provisioned tokens/sec = required tokens/sec * HF. Default HF values by class:
   - Tier-1 regions (NA-west, NA-east, EU-west): HF = 1.45 (target for public multi-tenant SLA)
   - Tier-2 regions (APAC, SA): HF = 1.30
   - Experimental / low-traffic regions: HF = 1.20
5) Convert tokens/sec to GPU count in each region: GPUs_needed = ceil(provisioned_tokens / UGC[chosen_GPU_type] / target_utilization_scaling) where target_utilization_scaling = 0.72 (we cap steady-state utilization to ~72% to leave thermal/autoscale headroom).

Sample calculation (NA-east, December observed peak):
- T30-95 observed tokens/sec = 4,800,000 tokens/sec (5-minute peak aggregate).
- Growth g = 1.12 -> required = 5,376,000 tokens/sec.
- HF for Tier-1 = 1.45 -> provisioned = 7,795,200 tokens/sec.
- Choose H100 UGC = 22,000 tokens/sec.
- Target scaling factor = 0.72 -> effective per-GPU = 15,840 tokens/sec.
- GPUs_needed = ceil(7,795,200 / 15,840) = ceil(492.2) = 493 GPUs.
Notes: round GPUs to nearest rack increment (e.g., multiples of 8/16) during procurement.

QPS mapping and conversion notes:
- QPS is useful for routing decisions but token-based sizing is primary. For capacity conversations we translate QPS -> tokens/sec using model-weighted avg tokens/request.
- Example mapping: if avg tokens per request = 120, tokens/sec_target = QPS * 120 / average_generation_latency_seconds. For planning we prefer tokens/sec measured directly from telemetry.

Steady-state utilization targets and cost tradeoffs:
- Target steady-state utilization: 55% - 72% of theoretical GPU throughput (lower end for Tier-1 when we want lower latency variance).
- Economic target: aim to keep effective tokens-per-dollar within 10% of the global average. If a region is >15% worse, prefer cross-region routing or cold standby models rather than buying more GPUs.

Emergency headroom and short-term surge policy:
- Immediate surge handling (0-20 min):
  - Traffic up to HF * required can be covered by existing reserved capacity + rapid autoscale burst pools (spot or burst instances).
  - If utilization >95% on all primary region GPUs, begin failover to secondary region pair with lower HF and warm standby.
- Sustained surge (>20 min up to 6 hours):
  - Engage transient capacity purchases (cloud GPU spare inventory) and activate fast-rollback canaries for model variants with smaller UGC (reduce per-request tokens).
  - Rate-limit non-critical routes and reduce default sampling/temperature for experimental customers (customer-facing knobs in Console).
- Post-surge: run retrospective to adjust HF and g assumptions if surge was substantive.

Autoscaling policy recommendations (region control plane):
- Scale-in/out triggers use tokens/sec moving average over 60s and 5m windows plus p95 latency guardrails.
- Minimum reserve: keep at least 8 GPUs warm per region (or 1 rack equivalent) to avoid cold-start tail latency for the first concurrent requests.
- Burst pool: configured to attach up to 30% additional GPUs for Tier-1 regions with <10 min spin-up.

GPU fleet allocation guidance (procurement vs cloud):
- Mix target (Tier-1): 60% owned/reserved (dedicated contracts), 40% on-demand for bursts. This balances cost and headroom agility.
- For EU/NA Tier-1 prioritize H100 if price delta < 20% because of higher UGC and lower per-token latency variability.

Observability and alerting (what to monitor):
- Telemetry signals: region_tokens_1m, region_tokens_5m_p95, gpu_utilization_p95, p99_latency_tokens, queue_depth, model_kv_cache_hit_rate, average_tokens_per_request_by_model.
- Alerts:
  - P1: region_tokens_5m_p95 > provisioned_tokens * 0.95 AND gpu_utilization_p95 > 88% -> emergency paging (SRE).
  - P2: sustained tokens_30m_avg growth > 20% vs previous 30m baseline -> ops channel and cross-functional review.
  - P3: model_kv_cache_hit_rate drops > 10% -> investigate routing or model config changes.

Operational runbook snippets (short actionable steps):
- If P1 fires:
  1) Confirm telemetry (region + global).
  2) Switch non-critical traffic to lower-cost regions via priority routing (Console -> routing profile: failover -> region B).
  3) Trigger burst capacity (cloud provider API) and enable faster autoscale intervals.
  4) Post-mortem: attach surge snapshots to the ticket and label with root cause hypothesis.

- If sustained >3x baseline for >1 hour and costs exceed thresholds:
  1) Throttle experimental projects (tagged in product metadata).
  2) Roll out a smaller quantized model variant to reduce per-token cost; use canary rollouts to verify quality impact.

Quality and regression considerations:
- Any change that increases HF or adds GPUs should be paired with a quality check: run a standard prompt sweep and ensure p95 response quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim) are within acceptable delta.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should HF be dynamic by customer class (we currently use region-tiered HF)? Decision point: pros/cons of customer-tier HF (custom SLAs) vs simpler region-only HF.
- How to integrate multi-model KV cache sharing into UGC calculations (savings when many small requests hit same cache).

Appendix A: Quick-reference cheat sheet
- HF defaults: Tier-1 1.45, Tier-2 1.30, Experimental 1.20
- Target steady-state utilization: 55% - 72%
- Minimum warm GPUs per region: 8
- Growth assumption for next quarter: g = 1.12/mo (adjust per product signals)
- Monitoring: region_tokens_5m_p95, gpu_utilization_p95, p99_latency_tokens

Appendix B: Example region table (simplified)
Region | T30-95 tokens/sec | required (g=1.12) | provisioned (HF) | GPU type | UGC eff | GPUs
NA-east | 4,800,000 | 5,376,000 | 7,795,200 | H100 | 15,840 | 493
EU-west | 3,200,000 | 3,584,000 | 5,196,800 | H100 | 15,840 | 328
APAC | 1,100,000 | 1,232,000 | 1,601,600 | A100 | 10,080 | 159

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Ava Martinez (eng-infrastructure).
- Review cadence: quarterly and after any significant surge incident.
- Suggested next steps: validate UGC numbers per model with perf team (action owner: Ravi Patel, due in 2 weeks).

This playbook is intentionally operational and concise — use it as the source of truth for capacity conversations and put long-form modeling spreadsheets in the linked Confluence artifact (CONFLUENCE-1234).
